fields.why: Besides the 1988-1998 contrasts, the notice gives single-quantity figures (15,935 deaths and ~305,000 injuries in 1998), which are summaries; B listed only comparison.

The notice runs no study of its own; the 1988-1998 decline is cited from references 1-2, so adding 'before/after or trend' describes cited content rather than the report's design. A's reading follows the 'two time points' rule and is defensible, but B's single value fits a limited-data notice better.

brief_issues: The study_design list has no value for an awareness-month notice or announcement; 'guidance or recommendations' is used by default although this notice gives no guidance. A rule could say: announcements -> 'mixed/other' (or add 'notice/announcement'), and designs are not inferred from figures cited from other reports.
